edition: Alberta Driver’s Guide: Cars and light trucks (2026)

questions.q: What is the minimum score needed to pass the Alberta Class 7 knowledge test?
o: 20 out of 30
23 out of 30
25 out of 30
28 out of 30
questions.e: You need 25 out of 30 (83%) correct.

questions.q: As a Class 7 learner, what blood alcohol level are you allowed while driving?
o: Under 0.05
Under 0.08
0.00 — zero
One drink is fine
questions.e: Class 7 learners must be at zero (0.00). The same zero rule covers cannabis and other drugs.

questions.q: A Class 7 learner must be accompanied by a supervising driver who is:
o: Any licensed driver
Fully licensed, 18 or older, in the front passenger seat
A GDL driver in the back seat
At least 16 years old
questions.e: Your supervisor must be a fully licensed (non-GDL) driver, 18+, seated beside you in front.

questions.q: At how many demerit points is a Class 7 learner's licence suspended?
o: 6 points
8 points
12 points
15 points
questions.e: GDL drivers are suspended at 8 demerit points — lower than the 15 for fully licensed drivers.

questions.q: A Class 7 learner is NOT permitted to drive between:
o: 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
Midnight and 5 a.m.
11 p.m. and 4 a.m.
Sunset and sunrise
questions.e: Learners may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.

questions.q: How often may you attempt the Alberta driver knowledge test?
o: Twice in a 24-hour period
Once per day
Once every 7 days
Three times per calendar month
questions.e: The knowledge test may be taken once per day, and the fee must be paid for each attempt.

questions.q: Can a Class 7 learner upgrade to a commercial licence (Class 1, 2, 3 or 4)?
o: Yes, anytime
No — not while in GDL
Yes, after passing a test
Only Class 4
questions.e: GDL drivers cannot hold or upgrade to a commercial licence.

questions.q: When can a Class 7 learner drive alone?
o: After holding the licence for 6 months
Never — a qualified supervising driver is required
After turning 16, but only during daylight hours
After completing an approved driver-training course
questions.e: A Class 7 learner can never drive alone; a qualified supervisor must always be beside you.

questions.q: To exit the GDL program and get a full Class 5 licence, you must first:
o: Be at least 18, complete the required probationary period, and be suspension- and demerit-free for the last 12 months
Pass an advanced road test after holding a Class 5-GDL licence for one year
Hold a Class 7 licence for 24 months without taking a Class 5 road test
Complete a commercial driver-training course and turn 18
questions.e: To exit GDL, you must be at least 18, complete the required probationary period, and be suspension- and demerit-free for the last 12 months. An advanced road test is no longer required.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to get a Class 7 learner's licence in Alberta?
questions.e: You can get a Class 7 licence at 14 (with parent/guardian consent if under 18).

questions.q: If you are under 18, what else do you need to apply for a Class 7 licence?
o: A job
Parent or guardian consent
A vehicle of your own
Two references
questions.e: Applicants under 18 need written parental or guardian consent.

questions.q: Can a Class 7 learner act as the supervising driver for another learner?
o: Yes
No
Only a family member
Only in daytime
questions.e: A GDL driver cannot supervise another learner — the supervisor must be fully licensed.

questions.q: The Class 7 knowledge test also requires you to pass a:
o: Hearing test
Vision test
Physical fitness test
Written essay
questions.e: You must pass a vision test along with the knowledge test.

questions.q: Besides alcohol, the zero-tolerance rule for Class 7 learners also covers:
o: Coffee
Cannabis and other impairing drugs
Energy drinks
Prescription vitamins
questions.e: Zero tolerance applies to cannabis and other impairing drugs too, not just alcohol.

questions.q: What is the speed limit in a school zone unless otherwise posted?
o: 20 km/h
30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
questions.e: School zones are 30 km/h (urban and rural) unless a sign posts otherwise.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta school zone sign with maximum 30 km/h

questions.q: What is the speed limit in a playground zone when in effect?
o: 25 km/h
30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
questions.e: Playground zones are 30 km/h unless otherwise posted.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta playground zone sign with maximum 30 km/h

questions.q: When are playground zone speed limits in effect?
o: Only on school days during the hours posted below the sign
Every day from 8:30 a.m. until one hour after sunset, unless local signs state different hours
Every day from 7:30 a.m. until 9:00 p.m. throughout Alberta
At all times, unless an end-of-zone sign is posted
questions.e: Playground zones apply every day, 8:30 a.m. to one hour after sunset.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta playground zone sign with maximum 30 km/h

questions.q: The default speed limit in an urban area (no posted sign) is:
o: 30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
60 km/h
questions.e: Unless posted otherwise, the urban default is 50 km/h.

questions.q: You may pass another vehicle in a school or playground zone when the zone is in effect:
o: Only when both vehicles are below 30 km/h
Never — passing a vehicle travelling in the same direction is not allowed
Only when the vehicle ahead is turning right
Only when there are two marked lanes in your direction
questions.e: You must not pass another vehicle in a school or playground zone while the limit is in effect.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta playground zone sign with maximum 30 km/h

questions.q: A school zone speed limit applies:
o: 24 hours a day
On school days during posted hours
Only in winter
Only when a crossing guard is present
questions.e: School zone limits apply on school days during the posted hours.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta school zone sign with maximum 30 km/h

questions.q: You see a playground sign with no speed limit attached. This means:
o: You are entering a 30 km/h playground zone immediately
You are entering a playground area — use caution because children may be nearby
The reduced speed applies only during school hours
You have reached the end of a playground zone
questions.e: A playground sign without a speed sign warns you're entering a playground area; drive with caution.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta playground area warning sign

questions.q: If you are caught speeding in a construction zone with workers present, penalties are usually:
o: The same as elsewhere unless a flag person is present
Doubled or otherwise increased
Reduced when traffic is light
Applied only if the temporary speed is below 50 km/h
questions.e: Fines are typically increased in construction zones when workers are present.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta road work warning sign

questions.q: On most open rural highways in Alberta, the speed limit is commonly:
o: 50 km/h
60 km/h
120 km/h
questions.e: Rural highways are commonly 80 to 100 km/h, depending on the road and posted signs.

questions.q: What must a driver do at this sign?
o: Slow and yield only when traffic is present
Come to a complete stop and proceed only when safe
Stop only if another road user has the right of way
Reduce speed and continue without stopping if the intersection is clear
questions.e: A STOP sign requires a complete stop. Proceed only after yielding and confirming the way is safe.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta STOP sign

questions.q: What must a driver do when approaching this sign?
o: Always come to a complete stop before continuing
Yield the right-of-way, slowing or stopping when necessary
Continue because traffic on this approach has priority
Stop only when a pedestrian is present
questions.e: A YIELD sign requires you to give the right-of-way. Slow down and stop when necessary before entering.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta yield sign

questions.q: What category of information does this sign provide?
o: A regulation that must always be obeyed
Advance warning of a road condition or hazard
Directions, routes, or distances to a destination
The location of a service available to drivers
questions.e: Yellow diamond signs warn of road conditions or hazards ahead. This example warns of a sharp right turn.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta sharp right turn warning sign

questions.q: What does this orange sign warn drivers about?
o: A permanent change in the highway alignment
Construction or maintenance work ahead
A school or playground crossing
A route reserved for slow-moving vehicles
questions.e: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used for construction, maintenance, and work zones.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta road work warning sign

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign warn drivers about?
o: A hospital or emergency service entrance
A school area or school crossing
A playground zone that is always 30 km/h
A pedestrian crossing controlled by traffic lights
questions.e: The five-sided school sign warns that children may be walking along or crossing the road.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta school area sign

questions.q: What type of sign is shown?
o: Warning sign describing a possible hazard
Regulatory sign stating a rule that must be obeyed
Guide sign showing destinations and distances
Service sign identifying facilities for drivers
questions.e: White rectangular signs such as maximum-speed signs are regulatory signs and state rules that drivers must obey.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta maximum speed regulatory sign

questions.q: What information does this green highway sign provide?
o: Advance warning of a road hazard or curve
Directions, distances, routes, or destinations
A regulatory rule such as a maximum speed
Information about construction and temporary detours
questions.e: Green guide signs provide route, direction, destination, and distance information.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta green destination and distance sign

questions.q: What service does this green sign indicate?
o: A highway information centre
A hospital
A hotel or lodging area
A helicopter landing area
questions.e: The white H service symbol indicates a hospital. In the Alberta driver's guide, it is shown on a green service sign.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta hospital service sign

questions.q: What must a driver do at this flashing signal?
o: Yield without stopping when the intersection appears clear
Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe
Remain stopped until the signal changes to steady green
Stop only when cross traffic is present
questions.e: Treat a flashing red signal like a stop sign: make a full stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta flashing red traffic signal illustration

questions.q: What must a driver do at this flashing signal?
o: Stop, then proceed as at a four-way stop
Slow down and proceed with caution
Continue at the posted speed because you have priority
Yield only to vehicles approaching from the right
questions.e: A flashing amber signal means slow down, check the intersection, and proceed cautiously.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta flashing amber traffic signal illustration

questions.q: The traffic signal changes to the steady yellow indication shown. What should you do?
o: Accelerate if you believe you can enter before the red light
Stop if you can do so safely
Brake immediately even if an abrupt stop may cause a collision
Continue at the same speed because yellow gives full right-of-way
questions.e: A steady yellow signal warns that red is coming. Stop before entering if you can do so safely.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta steady yellow traffic signal illustration

questions.q: What do the solid yellow centre lines shown mean?
o: Passing is permitted in either direction when the road is clear
Passing is not permitted in either direction
Traffic on both sides travels in the same direction
The space between the lines is a two-way left-turn lane
questions.e: Single or double solid yellow centre lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is not permitted.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta solid yellow centre line illustration

questions.q: What does the red circle and diagonal slash on this sign mean?
o: The movement shown is mandatory
The movement shown is prohibited
The movement is allowed after yielding
The restriction applies only during posted hours
questions.e: A red circle and diagonal slash mean the action or movement shown is prohibited.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta prohibited left turn sign

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
o: Turning left at the intersection
Making a U-turn
Entering a divided roadway
Using the intersection to reverse direction only during heavy traffic
questions.e: This sign prohibits U-turns at that location.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta no U-turn sign

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
o: Traffic may travel in one direction only
Do not enter from your direction
Yield before entering the roadway
The road is closed only to commercial vehicles
questions.e: The red circle with the horizontal white bar means do not enter from your direction.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta do not enter sign

questions.q: What may a driver do at the steady green signal shown?
o: Proceed when safe, yielding to pedestrians and traffic still lawfully in the intersection
Proceed immediately because all other road users must stop
Proceed straight only; every turn requires a green arrow
Enter only after stopping and checking both directions
questions.e: A steady green permits you to proceed when safe, but you must still yield to pedestrians and anyone lawfully in the intersection.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta steady green traffic signal illustration

questions.q: What does the green left arrow shown permit?
o: A protected left turn in the arrow's direction
A left turn after yielding to oncoming traffic
A left turn only after coming to a full stop
A U-turn but not a left turn
questions.e: A green arrow permits a protected movement in the arrow's direction. Conflicting traffic is stopped.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta green left arrow traffic signal illustration

questions.q: What does the white diamond pavement marking shown usually indicate?
o: A lane intended primarily for passing
A reserved lane, such as an HOV, bus, or bicycle lane
A lane where curbside parking is permitted
A lane that must be used by turning vehicles
questions.e: White diamond pavement markings indicate a reserved lane. Nearby signs specify which vehicles and times apply.
questions.imgAlt: Official Alberta white diamond reserved-lane pavement marking

questions.q: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who yields?
o: The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right
The vehicle turning right yields to the vehicle travelling straight
The vehicle on the narrower road has the right of way
questions.e: Yield to the vehicle on your right when you arrive together with no signs or lights.

questions.q: You want to make a left turn at a plain green light. You should:
o: Begin the turn before oncoming traffic enters the intersection
Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then turn when clear
Wait in the crosswalk until the signal turns yellow
Turn at the same time as opposing right-turning traffic
questions.e: On a plain green, a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

questions.q: A pedestrian is waiting at a marked crosswalk. You should:
o: Continue if the pedestrian has not stepped off the curb
Stop and allow the pedestrian to cross
Slow down but continue if your lane is clear
Stop only when the pedestrian reaches your half of the roadway
questions.e: Yield and stop for pedestrians at a crosswalk.

questions.q: At a four-way stop, right of way goes to:
o: The biggest vehicle
Whoever arrived and stopped first
The vehicle turning left
The fastest to react
questions.e: The vehicle that stops first goes first; if tied, yield to the right.

questions.q: In a roundabout (traffic circle), you should:
o: Enter at traffic speed because vehicles inside must yield
Yield to traffic already circulating, then enter when a safe gap is available
Come to a full stop before entering, even when the circle is empty
Enter to the left and travel clockwise around the centre island
questions.e: Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout, then enter on a safe gap.

questions.q: You're turning left into a driveway across oncoming traffic. You must yield to:
o: Nobody
Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians
Only large trucks
Only cyclists
questions.e: A left turn must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians where you're turning.

questions.q: When entering a highway from an on-ramp, you should:
o: Enter below highway speed and accelerate after changing lanes
Match the speed of traffic and merge into a safe gap
Stop near the end of the acceleration lane until both lanes are clear
Continue along the shoulder until another driver creates a gap
questions.e: Use the ramp to reach traffic speed, then merge smoothly into a gap.

questions.q: A funeral procession is passing through an intersection. You should:
o: Enter through a large gap if your light is green
Wait and allow the procession to continue
Join the procession briefly to cross the intersection
Proceed when the lead vehicle has passed, regardless of following vehicles
questions.e: Yield to a funeral procession and don't break into it.

questions.q: You reach a stop sign at the same time as a pedestrian starting to cross. You should:
o: Go first
Let the pedestrian cross
Wave them back
Edge forward
questions.e: Pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk have the right of way.

questions.q: When a vehicle ahead is stopped to let a pedestrian cross, drivers behind should:
o: Pass only after changing to the lane farthest from the pedestrian
Also stop and not pass the stopped vehicle
Proceed slowly if the pedestrian is not visible
Pass when the stopped driver signals that the lane is clear
questions.e: Never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian — someone may be crossing you can't see.

questions.q: A school bus ahead has its RED lights flashing. You must:
o: Stop only when you are travelling behind the bus
Stop whether approaching or following, unless separated by a physical median
Slow to 30 km/h and pass when no children are visible
Stop only while the bus door is open
questions.e: Stop for flashing red lights from either direction. Exception: the bus is across a physically divided (median) highway.

questions.q: A school bus ahead turns on its flashing AMBER (yellow) lights. This means:
o: The bus is about to re-enter traffic
Be prepared to stop because the red lights will follow
Pass before the bus reaches its stopping point
Stop immediately in your lane before reaching the bus
questions.e: Amber flashing lights are a warning: get ready to stop. Red lights come next as it stops.

questions.q: When do you NOT have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
o: When you are approaching from the opposite direction on any four-lane road
When the bus is on the opposite side of a highway divided by a physical median
When the bus is stopped at a marked bus bay
When all children have reached the sidewalk
questions.e: The only exception is when the bus is on the opposite side of a highway divided by a physical median.

questions.q: The penalty for illegally passing a school bus with red lights flashing includes:
o: A warning only
A fine plus demerit points
1 demerit point only
Loss of licence for a year
questions.e: It's a serious offence carrying a fine plus demerit points.

questions.q: After a school bus's red lights stop flashing, you may:
o: Proceed as soon as the stop arm begins retracting
Proceed with caution after confirming the way is clear
Pass only after the bus begins moving
Proceed without checking because children no longer have right of way
questions.e: Proceed only once the red lights stop flashing, watching for children still nearby.

questions.q: Even when a school bus has no lights flashing, you should:
o: Treat it like any other vehicle and maintain normal following distance
Watch carefully for children who may be loading, unloading, or crossing
Pass whenever the bus travels below the posted speed
Remain stopped until the bus driver waves you through
questions.e: Stay alert for children loading, unloading, or crossing even if lights aren't flashing.

questions.q: An emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren on a two-way road. You should:
o: Continue to the next intersection before stopping
Pull as far right as practical and stop
Stop where you are, even if you block the travel lane
Move left if the emergency vehicle is approaching from behind
questions.e: Pull to the right and stop, clearing a path — no matter which direction it comes from.

questions.q: How closely may you follow an emergency vehicle running its lights and siren?
o: No closer than 60 m
No closer than 150 m
No closer than 500 m
You may follow directly behind
questions.e: Stay at least 150 metres back from a responding emergency vehicle.

questions.q: You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside. You should:
o: Maintain the posted speed if responders are outside your lane
Slow down and, when safe, move over to provide space
Stop beside the emergency vehicle and wait for directions
Move over without reducing speed
questions.e: Slow down and move over a lane if you safely can, to protect responders.

questions.q: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you're stopped in an intersection, you should:
o: Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle changes direction
Clear the intersection when safe, then pull right and stop
Reverse behind the stop line before yielding
Turn at the intersection even if the turn is not permitted
questions.e: Clear the intersection safely, then pull to the right and stop to let it pass.

questions.q: How far from a fire hydrant must you park (Alberta rules of the road)?
o: 1 metre
At least 5 metres
At least 15 metres
No restriction
questions.e: Do not park within 5 metres of a fire hydrant.

questions.q: How close to a marked crosswalk may you park?
o: No nearer than 1 metre
No nearer than 5 metres
No nearer than 10 metres
No nearer than 15 metres
questions.e: Do not park within 5 metres of the near side of a marked crosswalk.

questions.q: You may not park within how far of a stop sign or the corner of an intersection?
o: 1 metre
5 metres
20 metres
No limit
questions.e: Keep at least 5 metres from a stop/yield sign and from the corner at an intersection.

questions.q: Parking on a bridge or in an underpass/subway is:
o: Allowed if brief
Not permitted
Fine at night
Allowed with flashers
questions.e: You may not park on a bridge or in a subway/underpass or on their approaches.

questions.q: Before opening your car door into traffic, you should:
o: Check the mirror only because cyclists must avoid parked vehicles
Check for cyclists, traffic, and pedestrians before opening
Signal left before opening the door
Open the door slightly first so approaching traffic can see it
questions.e: Always check that it's safe — watch for cyclists and passing traffic — before opening a door.

questions.q: You may not park within about how far of an access to a driveway or private road?
o: 1.5 metres
10 metres
25 metres
No restriction
questions.e: Do not park within 1.5 metres of a driveway or private road access.

questions.q: When parking facing downhill with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
o: Toward the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
It doesn't matter
questions.e: Downhill, turn wheels toward the curb so the car rolls into it if the brakes slip.

questions.q: When you leave your parked vehicle, you should:
o: Shift to park but leave the parking brake released on level ground
Set the parking brake, secure the transmission, and remove the key
Set the parking brake but leave the key in case the vehicle must be moved
Use the hazard lights instead of the parking brake for short stops
questions.e: Set the parking brake, shift to park, remove the key, and lock up.

questions.q: What is a safe following distance in good conditions?
o: Half a car length
At least a 2-second gap
One car length at any speed
5 metres
questions.e: Keep at least a 2-second gap — more in poor weather — so you have time to react.

questions.q: In rain, snow, or fog you should increase your following distance to:
o: Exactly 2 seconds because lower speed provides enough stopping room
At least 3 to 4 seconds or more, depending on conditions
Exactly 5 seconds in every type of poor weather
One additional vehicle length regardless of speed
questions.e: Bad conditions need a larger gap — 3 to 4 seconds or more.

questions.q: When must you turn your headlights on?
o: From sunset until sunrise, but not during poor daytime visibility
From one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise, and whenever visibility is poor
From one hour before sunset until one hour after sunrise in all conditions
Only when street lighting is not available
questions.e: Headlights are required during nighttime — one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise — and whenever conditions reduce visibility.

questions.q: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
o: Brake firmly and steer opposite the direction you want to travel
Ease off the accelerator and steer where you want the vehicle to go
Accelerate gently until the tires regain traction
Hold the steering wheel straight until the vehicle stops sliding
questions.e: Ease off the accelerator and steer where you want the front to go; avoid slamming the brakes.

questions.q: On a slippery or icy road, you should:
o: Use firm, repeated braking to test available traction
Slow down and increase your following distance
Maintain the posted speed but avoid lane changes
Follow the vehicle ahead more closely so you can copy its path
questions.e: Slow down and leave extra distance — stopping takes much longer on ice.

questions.q: 'Hydroplaning' happens when:
o: Your engine overheats
Tires ride up on water and lose grip
You brake too gently
You use high beams
questions.e: Hydroplaning is when tires lose contact by riding on a film of water; ease off the gas and don't brake hard.

questions.q: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, you should:
o: Maintain speed so the tire tread clears water more quickly
Slow down and keep your tires properly inflated and in good condition
Brake lightly whenever you cross standing water
Steer toward the deepest tire tracks left by other vehicles
questions.e: Lower speed and good tires reduce hydroplaning risk.

questions.q: What should you check before changing lanes?
o: Mirrors only, provided they are adjusted correctly
Mirrors, signal, and a shoulder check of the blind spot
The lane ahead and the rear-view mirror only
The side mirror twice instead of performing a shoulder check
questions.e: Mirror, signal, then shoulder-check your blind spot before moving over.

questions.q: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots. The safest approach is:
o: Remain beside the cab where the driver is most likely to notice you
Avoid lingering beside them; if you cannot see the driver's mirror, the driver may not see you
Pass on the right because the driver sits on the left
Follow closely so your headlights remain visible in the mirrors
questions.e: Stay out of the 'No-Zones'. If you can't see the driver in their mirror, they can't see you.

questions.q: If you feel drowsy while driving, the safest thing is to:
o: Open a window and continue until the next scheduled stop
Pull over somewhere safe and rest
Drink caffeine and continue at a reduced speed
Change lanes frequently to stay mentally engaged
questions.e: Fatigue impairs driving — pull over and rest; music and air don't fix drowsiness.

questions.q: Using a hand-held cellphone while driving in Alberta is:
o: Permitted while fully stopped at a red traffic light
Illegal under distracted-driving law
Permitted for Class 5 drivers but not learners
Illegal only when the vehicle is travelling above 50 km/h
questions.e: Hand-held phone use is distracted driving — illegal, with a fine and demerit points.

questions.q: When approaching a railway crossing with flashing red lights, you must:
o: Cross if the train is still more than one block away
Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed
Slow to 30 km/h and cross after checking both directions
Stop only when the crossing gate has lowered
questions.e: Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the way is clear — never try to beat a train.

questions.q: Before starting to drive, your first actions should be to:
o: Start moving, then adjust the mirrors once traffic is clear
Fasten your seatbelt and adjust your seat and mirrors
Check the dashboard after entering the roadway
Adjust only the rear-view mirror because side mirrors are checked while moving
questions.e: Buckle up and adjust your seat and mirrors before you move.

questions.q: The safest way to handle a tailgater behind you is to:
o: Tap the brakes to show that the following distance is unsafe
Move over when safe and allow the vehicle to pass
Increase speed until a larger gap develops behind you
Maintain position and focus only on traffic ahead
questions.e: Let a tailgater pass when you safely can; don't brake-check or race.

questions.q: When driving in fog, you should use:
o: High-beam headlights to illuminate farther ahead
Low-beam headlights to reduce reflected glare
Parking lights so other drivers can see your vehicle
Hazard lights together with high-beam headlights
questions.e: Low beams work better in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

questions.q: The recommended way to steer in normal driving is:
o: One hand near the 12 o’clock position
Both hands around 9 and 3, or another balanced low position
One hand low on the wheel while the other rests on the gear selector
Both hands close together at the top of the wheel
questions.e: Keep both hands on the wheel at balanced positions for control.

questions.q: 'Nighttime' in the Alberta Basic Licence Driver's Guide is defined as:
o: Sunset to sunrise
One hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
9 p.m. to 6 a.m.
When streetlights are on
questions.e: Officially, nighttime is one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise.

questions.q: You're being passed by another vehicle. You should:
o: Increase speed slightly so the passing vehicle spends less time beside you
Maintain a steady speed and allow the vehicle to complete the pass
Move toward the centre line to discourage an unsafe pass
Brake firmly as soon as the passing vehicle reaches your blind spot
questions.e: Hold your speed (or ease off slightly) so they can pass safely.

questions.q: Cruise control is best avoided on:
o: Dry highways
Wet, icy, or slippery roads
Long straight roads
Flat ground
questions.e: Avoid cruise control on slippery roads where you may need full control.

questions.q: When you plan to turn, you should signal:
o: Only after beginning to slow down
Well before the turn so other road users have time to react
Only when another vehicle is close enough to be affected
At the point where you begin turning the steering wheel
questions.e: Signal early, before slowing, to give others time to react.

questions.q: If your brakes suddenly fail, one thing you can try is:
o: Switch off the ignition immediately while travelling at speed
Pump the brake pedal and downshift to help reduce speed
Apply the parking brake fully in one motion
Shift directly into park while steering to the shoulder
questions.e: Pump the pedal, shift to a lower gear, and use the parking brake gently; steer to a safe spot.

questions.q: Your right wheels drift onto a soft shoulder. You should:
o: Steer sharply back onto the pavement before losing speed
Ease off the accelerator, slow down, and return gently to the road
Brake firmly while half of the vehicle remains on the pavement
Accelerate so the tires climb back over the pavement edge
questions.e: Don't jerk the wheel — slow down, then ease back onto the road smoothly.

questions.q: When you approach a curve, you should:
o: Maintain speed until entering the curve, then brake as needed
Slow before the curve, then accelerate gently through it
Coast through the curve with the transmission in neutral
Move toward the centre line to reduce the sharpness of the curve
questions.e: Reduce speed before the curve, then power gently through for control.

questions.q: The best defence against another driver's mistake is to:
o: Match the speed of surrounding traffic even when conditions are poor
Stay alert and maintain space around your vehicle
Follow closely enough to anticipate the other driver’s movement
Use the horn whenever another vehicle approaches your lane
questions.e: Defensive driving — space, attention, anticipating others — prevents most collisions.

questions.q: On a multi-lane road, slower traffic should generally keep:
o: Left
Right
Centre
Any lane
questions.e: Keep right except to pass; leave the left lane for passing.

questions.q: When you're the first to arrive at a collision scene, you should:
o: Continue driving and report the location at the next safe stop
Stop if safe, call for help, and warn approaching traffic
Move injured people away from the vehicles before calling for help
Park in the travel lane so other drivers are forced to slow down
questions.e: Stop if safe, call 911, and warn traffic; don't move the injured unless there's danger.

questions.q: How many passengers may a Class 7 learner carry?
o: No passengers at all
Only family members
No more than the number of seatbelts
Up to 4 friends
questions.e: No more passengers than there are working seatbelts in the vehicle.

questions.q: Who must wear a seatbelt in the vehicle?
o: Only the driver
Only front-seat riders
The driver and every passenger
Only passengers under 16
questions.e: The driver and all passengers must be properly buckled up.

questions.q: Who is legally responsible for making sure passengers under 16 are buckled up?
o: The passenger once they can fasten the belt without help
The driver of the vehicle
The registered owner, even when someone else is driving
The child’s parent or guardian, even when absent
questions.e: The driver is responsible for ensuring passengers under 16 are properly secured.

questions.q: In Alberta, a child must ride rear-facing until at least:
o: 1 year of age, regardless of the seat limits
2 years of age or until reaching the seat manufacturer's rear-facing limit
18 kg (40 lb), regardless of age
6 years of age or until a booster seat fits
questions.e: Children ride rear-facing until at least age 2 or the seat's stated height/weight limit.

questions.q: A forward-facing child car seat is required for children who are:
o: Under 6 years old, regardless of weight
Under 6 years old and 18 kg (40 lb) or less
Age 6 to 8 and shorter than 145 cm
Under 18 kg only when seated in the front passenger seat
questions.e: Children under 6 and under 18 kg (40 lb) must use a proper child car seat.

questions.q: Booster seats in Alberta are:
o: Required until a child reaches 145 cm
Strongly recommended until the seatbelt fits properly, but not required by Alberta law
Required for every child between ages 6 and 12
Required only when the vehicle has lap-and-shoulder belts
questions.e: Booster seats aren't legally required in Alberta but are strongly recommended until the belt fits properly.

questions.q: The safest place for children under 13 to ride is:
o: The front passenger seat with the seat moved fully rearward
The back seat, using the restraint appropriate for the child
Either front or back when a booster seat is being used
The front seat whenever the passenger airbag can be disabled
questions.e: Children are safest in the back seat, especially with front airbags.

questions.q: A seatbelt should be worn:
o: With the shoulder belt under the arm if it touches the neck
Across the chest and low across the hips
With the lap belt across the stomach and shoulder belt near the neck
Slightly loose so the body can move during a collision
questions.e: Wear the shoulder belt across the chest and the lap belt low and snug across the hips.

questions.q: Outside a city, town or village, what is the default maximum speed on a primary highway unless a sign states otherwise?
o: 80 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
questions.e: Unless a sign sets a different limit, the default maximum on a primary highway outside an urban area is 100 km/h.

questions.q: When backing a passenger vehicle to the left, where should the driver mainly look?
o: Over the left shoulder, with brief checks forward
Only in the left side mirror
Over the right shoulder for the entire manoeuvre
Only through the rear-view camera
questions.e: When backing left, look mainly over the left shoulder while making brief checks forward and around the vehicle.

questions.q: A green right-turn arrow is displayed beside a red traffic light. What may a driver do?
o: Turn right in the arrow's direction when the way is safe
Go straight after slowing
Turn right only after the signal becomes fully green
Make either a right or left turn after stopping
questions.e: A green arrow permits movement in the arrow's direction even when another signal is red, but the driver must still proceed safely and yield where required.

questions.q: A fully licensed Alberta driver normally receives a licence suspension after accumulating how many demerit points?
questions.e: A fully licensed driver is normally suspended at 15 demerit points. GDL drivers have a lower threshold.

questions.q: After passing a large truck on a two-way highway, when should you return to your lane?
o: As soon as your rear bumper clears the truck
After leaving extra space so the truck is clearly visible behind you
When the truck driver flashes the headlights
As soon as you can no longer see the truck's front wheels
questions.e: Large vehicles need more stopping room. Leave extra space before moving back into the lane ahead of a truck.

questions.q: Before turning right at a red light where the turn is permitted, what must you do?
o: Slow and turn without stopping when no vehicle is visible
Stop fully, check that the turn is permitted, yield, and turn only when safe
Stop only when pedestrians are present
Wait for a green light in every case
questions.e: A right turn on red requires a complete stop first. The driver must check for a prohibition and yield to traffic and pedestrians before turning.

questions.q: What does a single solid white line separating lanes generally tell drivers?
o: Traffic is moving in opposite directions
Lane changes across the line are not permitted
Passing must occur on the right
The lane is reserved only during rush hour
questions.e: A solid white line generally means drivers should not change lanes across it.

questions.q: In a vehicle equipped with ABS, what should you do during an emergency stop?
o: Pump the brake pedal rapidly
Press the brake firmly and keep steering toward a safe path
Apply the parking brake first
Release the brake whenever the pedal vibrates
questions.e: With ABS, apply firm continuous brake pressure and steer as needed. Pedal vibration is normal; do not pump the brakes.

questions.q: What does it mean to over-drive your headlights at night?
o: Using high beams longer than permitted
Driving too fast to stop within the distance illuminated ahead
Using headlights during daylight
Following another vehicle with headlights on
questions.e: You are over-driving your headlights when your stopping distance is longer than the distance you can see.

questions.q: When parallel parked, how close must the wheels nearest the curb generally be?
o: Within 20 cm
Within 30 cm
Within 50 cm
Within 1 metre
questions.e: When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the curb should be no more than 50 centimetres from it.

questions.q: When stopped behind another vehicle in traffic, what space should you leave?
o: Enough to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead and move out without reversing
Exactly one metre in all conditions
No more than half a vehicle length
Enough to see only the rear licence plate
questions.e: Leave enough room to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead and to move around it without first reversing.

questions.q: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is intended for vehicles that normally travel at less than:
o: 30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
60 km/h
questions.e: The slow-moving vehicle emblem identifies vehicles that normally travel at less than 40 km/h.

questions.q: What is a weave zone on a freeway?
o: A section where entrance and exit traffic must cross paths over a short distance
A series of sharp curves requiring alternating steering
A lane reserved for emergency vehicles
A shoulder area used by disabled vehicles
questions.e: A weave zone occurs where vehicles entering and leaving the freeway must cross paths within a limited distance.

questions.q: A registry road test may be refused when the test vehicle is:
o: A rental vehicle
More than five years old
Mechanically unsafe
Equipped with an automatic transmission
questions.e: The vehicle used for a road test must be safe and roadworthy. An examiner may refuse an unsafe vehicle.

questions.q: May a driver exceed the posted speed limit while passing another vehicle?
o: Yes, by up to 10 km/h
Yes, but only on a divided highway
No, the speed limit still applies
Only when the passing lane is short
questions.e: The posted speed limit remains the maximum legal speed while passing.

questions.q: When must a posted construction-zone speed limit be obeyed?
o: Only while workers are visible
Only during daylight hours
Whenever the limit is posted and in effect
Only while a flag person is controlling traffic
questions.e: Drivers must obey the posted construction-zone speed limit whenever it is in effect, not only when workers are visible.

questions.q: In a vehicle without ABS, what is threshold braking?
o: Pumping the brake pedal as rapidly as possible
Applying firm pressure just short of locking the wheels
Using only the parking brake
Locking the wheels and holding them locked
questions.e: Threshold braking uses the greatest braking force possible without locking the wheels.

questions.q: Which technique produces a smooth normal stop?
o: Increase brake pressure continuously until the vehicle stops
Brake firmly, ease pressure slightly near the end, then finish the stop
Shift to neutral before touching the brake
Pump the brake pedal throughout the stop
questions.e: For a smooth stop, apply the brakes, ease pressure slightly just before stopping, then finish the stop gently.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a freeway deceleration lane?
o: To build speed before entering the freeway
To reduce speed after leaving the through lane
To provide a lane for passing slow traffic
To stop and wait for a gap in freeway traffic
questions.e: Move into the deceleration lane before slowing so through traffic can continue at freeway speed.

questions.q: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road, which lane should you normally enter?
o: The lane nearest the right curb
The lane nearest the left curb
Any lane that appears clear
The centre lane when one exists
questions.e: A left turn from a two-way road onto a one-way road should normally finish in the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.q: When backing straight, where should the driver mainly look?
o: Over the right shoulder through the rear window, while checking around the vehicle
Only at the rear-view camera
Over the left shoulder at all times
Only in both side mirrors
questions.e: For straight backing, look mainly through the rear window over the right shoulder while continuing to check the vehicle's surroundings.

questions.q: What is an acceleration lane designed for?
o: Stopping before entering a freeway
Building speed to match freeway traffic before merging
Passing vehicles already on the freeway
Reducing speed before an exit
questions.e: Use an acceleration lane to reach a speed close to freeway traffic before merging into a safe gap.

questions.q: Unless signs state different times, when are Alberta school-zone limits generally in effect on school days?
o: 8:30 a.m. until one hour after sunset
From sunrise to sunset
Continuously from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
questions.e: Unless otherwise posted, the standard school-zone periods are 8:00–9:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m., and 3:00–4:30 p.m. on school days.

questions.q: A vehicle is trying to merge from an acceleration lane on your right. What should you do when possible?
o: Speed up to prevent it entering ahead
Maintain exactly the same position regardless of traffic
Move left if safe or adjust speed to help create a gap
Stop in the through lane
questions.e: Although the merging driver must find a safe gap, through drivers can improve safety by moving left when safe or adjusting speed.

questions.q: When parking uphill beside a curb, which way should the front wheels be turned?
o: Toward the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
Parallel to the curb
questions.e: Uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle would roll back against the curb if it moved.

questions.q: In normal urban driving, how far ahead should a driver generally scan?
o: About 3 to 5 seconds
About 6 to 8 seconds
About 12 to 15 seconds
At least 30 seconds
questions.e: Looking about 12 to 15 seconds ahead helps a driver identify hazards early and plan smoothly.

questions.q: As you approach the crest of a hill on a two-lane highway, where should you position your vehicle?
o: Close to the centre line
Toward the right side of your lane
Partly on the shoulder
In the oncoming lane if it appears clear
questions.e: Stay well to the right near a hill crest because an oncoming hazard may be hidden from view.

questions.q: What causes most vehicle skids?
o: Mechanical brake failure
Poor road design
Driver actions that exceed available traction
Snowfall by itself
questions.e: Most skids result from driver error, such as braking, steering, or accelerating too aggressively for available traction.

questions.q: When may a vehicle legally occupy a designated disability parking space?
o: Whenever the driver remains inside
When nearby spaces are full
When it displays the proper disability placard or licence plate
For any stop shorter than five minutes
questions.e: A designated disability space may be used only by a vehicle displaying the required valid placard or plate.

questions.q: At night, when following another vehicle, high beams should be dimmed when you are within approximately:
o: 60 metres
100 metres
150 metres
300 metres
questions.e: Dim high beams when following another vehicle within 150 metres so glare does not interfere with the other driver.

questions.q: When are dual turns from more than one lane permitted?
o: Whenever both roads have multiple lanes
Only when signs or pavement markings indicate them
Whenever traffic is light
Only when directed by another driver
questions.e: Dual turns are permitted only where signs or pavement markings specifically authorize them.

questions.q: What does a posted speed limit represent?
o: The speed every vehicle must maintain
The maximum speed under favourable road and weather conditions
A minimum speed for the lane
A limit that may be exceeded while passing
questions.e: A posted limit is the maximum under favourable conditions. Drivers must slow further when conditions make that speed unsafe.

questions.q: What makes an intersection uncontrolled?
o: It has traffic lights but no signs
It has stop signs on only one road
It has no traffic signs or traffic signals controlling right-of-way
It is controlled only during rush hour
questions.e: An uncontrolled intersection has no signs or signals assigning right-of-way. Drivers must apply the uncontrolled-intersection rules.

questions.q: At night, high beams must be dimmed for an approaching vehicle when it is within approximately:
o: 60 metres
150 metres
300 metres
500 metres
questions.e: Dim high beams when an approaching vehicle is within 300 metres to avoid blinding the other driver.

questions.q: Where should the centre of an adjustable head restraint be positioned?
o: At shoulder height
Near the top of the ears
At the base of the neck
Above the top of the head
questions.e: Position the centre of the head restraint near the top of the ears to reduce neck injury in a collision.

questions.q: A slower vehicle reaches a passing-lane section. What should its driver do?
o: Stay in the left lane to prevent unsafe passing
Move to the right lane when safe and allow faster traffic to pass
Increase speed above the limit
Stop on the shoulder until all traffic passes
questions.e: Slower traffic should use the right lane in a passing-lane section and allow faster vehicles to pass safely.

questions.q: Before driving from a parking lot or driveway across a sidewalk and onto a roadway, a driver must:
o: Stop only if a sign is posted
Come to a complete stop and yield before entering
Continue slowly because roadway traffic must yield
Stop only when a pedestrian is visible
questions.e: A driver emerging from a parking lot, alley, or driveway must stop before crossing the sidewalk or entering the roadway and yield as required.

questions.q: At a railway crossing with flashing red lights, how far from the nearest rail should you stop?
o: At least 2 metres
At least 3 metres
At least 5 metres
At least 15 metres
questions.e: Stop at least 5 metres from the nearest rail and wait until the warning stops and the crossing is safe.

questions.q: Why is it especially dangerous to pass a loaded log truck while it is turning?
o: The truck is not required to signal
The rear of the load can sweep across adjoining lanes
The truck must stop halfway through every turn
The driver cannot see vehicles in front
questions.e: The rear of a long load can swing or sweep across nearby lanes during a turn. Stay back and never try to squeeze past.

questions.q: When angle parked, how close should the front wheel be to the curb?
o: Within 25 cm
Within 50 cm
Within 75 cm
Within 1 metre
questions.e: When angle parked, the front wheel should be no more than 50 centimetres from the curb.

questions.q: A pedestrian at a crosswalk points an arm across the roadway. What should a driver understand?
o: The pedestrian is directing vehicles to continue
The pedestrian is indicating an intention to cross, so the driver must stop and yield
The pedestrian wants traffic to slow but not stop
The signal applies only to cyclists
questions.e: A pedestrian may signal an intention to cross by pointing an arm across the road. Drivers must stop and yield.

questions.q: A broken yellow centre line is beside a solid yellow line. When may you pass?
o: Only when the broken line is on your side and the pass is otherwise safe
Only when the solid line is on your side
From either direction whenever no vehicle is visible
Never from either direction
questions.e: Passing may be permitted for traffic beside the broken line, provided the manoeuvre is legal and safe. Traffic beside the solid line must not pass.

questions.q: On a two-lane highway, which side should normally be used to pass a vehicle travelling in the same direction?
o: The right side
The left side when the pass is legal and safe
Either shoulder
Whichever side has more space
questions.e: Normally pass on the left when markings, sight distance, and traffic conditions allow it safely.

questions.q: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, which way should the front wheels be turned?
o: Toward the right edge of the roadway
Toward the centre of the roadway
Straight ahead
Either direction if the parking brake is set
questions.e: Uphill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the right edge so the vehicle would roll away from traffic if it moved.

questions.q: Which option correctly states the minimum score needed to pass the Alberta Class 7 knowledge test?
o: 20 out of 30
23 out of 30
25 out of 30
28 out of 30
questions.e: You need 25 out of 30 (83%) correct.

questions.q: Under Alberta rules, as a Class 7 learner, what blood alcohol level are you allowed while driving?
o: Under 0.05
Under 0.08
0.00 — zero
One drink is fine
questions.e: Class 7 learners must be at zero (0.00). The same zero rule covers cannabis and other drugs.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A Class 7 learner must be accompanied by a supervising driver who is:
o: Any licensed driver
Fully licensed, 18 or older, in the front passenger seat
A GDL driver in the back seat
At least 16 years old
questions.e: Your supervisor must be a fully licensed (non-GDL) driver, 18+, seated beside you in front.

questions.q: Apply the correct Alberta rule. At how many demerit points is a Class 7 learner's licence suspended?
o: 6 points
8 points
12 points
15 points
questions.e: GDL drivers are suspended at 8 demerit points — lower than the 15 for fully licensed drivers.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A Class 7 learner is NOT permitted to drive between:
o: 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
Midnight and 5 a.m.
11 p.m. and 4 a.m.
Sunset and sunrise
questions.e: Learners may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.

questions.q: Which answer correctly gives the rule for often may you attempt the Alberta driver knowledge test?
o: Twice in a 24-hour period
Once per day
Once every 7 days
Three times per calendar month
questions.e: The knowledge test may be taken once per day, and the fee must be paid for each attempt.

questions.q: Under Alberta rules, can a Class 7 learner upgrade to a commercial licence (Class 1, 2, 3 or 4)?
o: Yes, anytime
No — not while in GDL
Yes, after passing a test
Only Class 4
questions.e: GDL drivers cannot hold or upgrade to a commercial licence.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When can a Class 7 learner drive alone?
o: After holding the licence for 6 months
Never — a qualified supervising driver is required
After turning 16, but only during daylight hours
After completing an approved driver-training course
questions.e: A Class 7 learner can never drive alone; a qualified supervisor must always be beside you.

questions.q: Which option correctly completes this safety rule? To exit the GDL program and get a full Class 5 licence, you must first:
o: Be at least 18, complete the required probationary period, and be suspension- and demerit-free for the last 12 months
Pass an advanced road test after holding a Class 5-GDL licence for one year
Hold a Class 7 licence for 24 months without taking a Class 5 road test
Complete a commercial driver-training course and turn 18
questions.e: To exit GDL, you must be at least 18, complete the required probationary period, and be suspension- and demerit-free for the last 12 months. An advanced road test is no longer required.

questions.q: Which option correctly states the minimum age to get a Class 7 learner's licence in Alberta?
questions.e: You can get a Class 7 licence at 14 (with parent/guardian consent if under 18).

questions.q: Apply the Alberta rule to this situation. If you are under 18, what else do you need to apply for a Class 7 licence?
o: A job
Parent or guardian consent
A vehicle of your own
Two references
questions.e: Applicants under 18 need written parental or guardian consent.

questions.q: Under Alberta rules, can a Class 7 learner act as the supervising driver for another learner?
o: Yes
No
Only a family member
Only in daytime
questions.e: A GDL driver cannot supervise another learner — the supervisor must be fully licensed.

questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The Class 7 knowledge test also requires you to pass a:
o: Hearing test
Vision test
Physical fitness test
Written essay
questions.e: You must pass a vision test along with the knowledge test.

questions.q: Which option correctly completes this licence condition? Besides alcohol, the zero-tolerance rule for Class 7 learners also covers:
o: Coffee
Cannabis and other impairing drugs
Energy drinks
Prescription vitamins
questions.e: Zero tolerance applies to cannabis and other impairing drugs too, not just alcohol.

questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The default speed limit in an urban area (no posted sign) is:
o: 30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
60 km/h
questions.e: Unless posted otherwise, the urban default is 50 km/h.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, on most open rural highways in Alberta, the speed limit is commonly:
o: 50 km/h
60 km/h
120 km/h
questions.e: Rural highways are commonly 80 to 100 km/h, depending on the road and posted signs.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who yields?
o: The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right
The vehicle turning right yields to the vehicle travelling straight
The vehicle on the narrower road has the right of way
questions.e: Yield to the vehicle on your right when you arrive together with no signs or lights.

questions.q: Imagine this occurs while you are driving. You want to make a left turn at a plain green light. You should:
o: Begin the turn before oncoming traffic enters the intersection
Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then turn when clear
Wait in the crosswalk until the signal turns yellow
Turn at the same time as opposing right-turning traffic
questions.e: On a plain green, a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A pedestrian is waiting at a marked crosswalk. You should:
o: Continue if the pedestrian has not stepped off the curb
Stop and allow the pedestrian to cross
Slow down but continue if your lane is clear
Stop only when the pedestrian reaches your half of the roadway
questions.e: Yield and stop for pedestrians at a crosswalk.

questions.q: Apply the correct Alberta rule. At a four-way stop, right of way goes to:
o: The biggest vehicle
Whoever arrived and stopped first
The vehicle turning left
The fastest to react
questions.e: The vehicle that stops first goes first; if tied, yield to the right.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, in a roundabout (traffic circle), you should:
o: Enter at traffic speed because vehicles inside must yield
Yield to traffic already circulating, then enter when a safe gap is available
Come to a full stop before entering, even when the circle is empty
Enter to the left and travel clockwise around the centre island
questions.e: Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout, then enter on a safe gap.

questions.q: While driving, you're turning left into a driveway across oncoming traffic. You must yield to:
o: Nobody
Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians
Only large trucks
Only cyclists
questions.e: A left turn must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians where you're turning.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When entering a highway from an on-ramp, you should:
o: Enter below highway speed and accelerate after changing lanes
Match the speed of traffic and merge into a safe gap
Stop near the end of the acceleration lane until both lanes are clear
Continue along the shoulder until another driver creates a gap
questions.e: Use the ramp to reach traffic speed, then merge smoothly into a gap.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A funeral procession is passing through an intersection. You should:
o: Enter through a large gap if your light is green
Wait and allow the procession to continue
Join the procession briefly to cross the intersection
Proceed when the lead vehicle has passed, regardless of following vehicles
questions.e: Yield to a funeral procession and don't break into it.

questions.q: Imagine this occurs while you are driving. You reach a stop sign at the same time as a pedestrian starting to cross. You should:
o: Go first
Let the pedestrian cross
Wave them back
Edge forward
questions.e: Pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk have the right of way.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When a vehicle ahead is stopped to let a pedestrian cross, drivers behind should:
o: Pass only after changing to the lane farthest from the pedestrian
Also stop and not pass the stopped vehicle
Proceed slowly if the pedestrian is not visible
Pass when the stopped driver signals that the lane is clear
questions.e: Never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian — someone may be crossing you can't see.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A school bus ahead has its RED lights flashing. You must:
o: Stop only when you are travelling behind the bus
Stop whether approaching or following, unless separated by a physical median
Slow to 30 km/h and pass when no children are visible
Stop only while the bus door is open
questions.e: Stop for flashing red lights from either direction. Exception: the bus is across a physically divided (median) highway.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A school bus ahead turns on its flashing AMBER (yellow) lights. This means:
o: The bus is about to re-enter traffic
Be prepared to stop because the red lights will follow
Pass before the bus reaches its stopping point
Stop immediately in your lane before reaching the bus
questions.e: Amber flashing lights are a warning: get ready to stop. Red lights come next as it stops.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When do you NOT have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
o: When you are approaching from the opposite direction on any four-lane road
When the bus is on the opposite side of a highway divided by a physical median
When the bus is stopped at a marked bus bay
When all children have reached the sidewalk
questions.e: The only exception is when the bus is on the opposite side of a highway divided by a physical median.

questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The penalty for illegally passing a school bus with red lights flashing includes:
o: A warning only
A fine plus demerit points
1 demerit point only
Loss of licence for a year
questions.e: It's a serious offence carrying a fine plus demerit points.

questions.q: After this event, which response is correct? After a school bus's red lights stop flashing, you may:
o: Proceed as soon as the stop arm begins retracting
Proceed with caution after confirming the way is clear
Pass only after the bus begins moving
Proceed without checking because children no longer have right of way
questions.e: Proceed only once the red lights stop flashing, watching for children still nearby.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, even when a school bus has no lights flashing, you should:
o: Treat it like any other vehicle and maintain normal following distance
Watch carefully for children who may be loading, unloading, or crossing
Pass whenever the bus travels below the posted speed
Remain stopped until the bus driver waves you through
questions.e: Stay alert for children loading, unloading, or crossing even if lights aren't flashing.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren on a two-way road. You should:
o: Continue to the next intersection before stopping
Pull as far right as practical and stop
Stop where you are, even if you block the travel lane
Move left if the emergency vehicle is approaching from behind
questions.e: Pull to the right and stop, clearing a path — no matter which direction it comes from.

questions.q: Which answer correctly gives the rule for closely may you follow an emergency vehicle running its lights and siren?
o: No closer than 60 m
No closer than 150 m
No closer than 500 m
You may follow directly behind
questions.e: Stay at least 150 metres back from a responding emergency vehicle.

questions.q: Imagine this occurs while you are driving. You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the roadside. You should:
o: Maintain the posted speed if responders are outside your lane
Slow down and, when safe, move over to provide space
Stop beside the emergency vehicle and wait for directions
Move over without reducing speed
questions.e: Slow down and move over a lane if you safely can, to protect responders.

questions.q: Apply the Alberta rule to this situation. If an emergency vehicle approaches while you're stopped in an intersection, you should:
o: Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle changes direction
Clear the intersection when safe, then pull right and stop
Reverse behind the stop line before yielding
Turn at the intersection even if the turn is not permitted
questions.e: Clear the intersection safely, then pull to the right and stop to let it pass.

questions.q: Which answer correctly gives the rule for far from a fire hydrant must you park (Alberta rules of the road)?
o: 1 metre
At least 5 metres
At least 15 metres
No restriction
questions.e: Do not park within 5 metres of a fire hydrant.

questions.q: Which answer correctly gives the rule for close to a marked crosswalk may you park?
o: No nearer than 1 metre
No nearer than 5 metres
No nearer than 10 metres
No nearer than 15 metres
questions.e: Do not park within 5 metres of the near side of a marked crosswalk.

questions.q: Imagine this occurs while you are driving. You may not park within how far of a stop sign or the corner of an intersection?
o: 1 metre
5 metres
20 metres
No limit
questions.e: Keep at least 5 metres from a stop/yield sign and from the corner at an intersection.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, parking on a bridge or in an underpass/subway is:
o: Allowed if brief
Not permitted
Fine at night
Allowed with flashers
questions.e: You may not park on a bridge or in a subway/underpass or on their approaches.

questions.q: Before this action, which requirement applies? Before opening your car door into traffic, you should:
o: Check the mirror only because cyclists must avoid parked vehicles
Check for cyclists, traffic, and pedestrians before opening
Signal left before opening the door
Open the door slightly first so approaching traffic can see it
questions.e: Always check that it's safe — watch for cyclists and passing traffic — before opening a door.

questions.q: Imagine this occurs while you are driving. You may not park within about how far of an access to a driveway or private road?
o: 1.5 metres
10 metres
25 metres
No restriction
questions.e: Do not park within 1.5 metres of a driveway or private road access.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When parking facing downhill with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
o: Toward the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
It doesn't matter
questions.e: Downhill, turn wheels toward the curb so the car rolls into it if the brakes slip.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When you leave your parked vehicle, you should:
o: Shift to park but leave the parking brake released on level ground
Set the parking brake, secure the transmission, and remove the key
Set the parking brake but leave the key in case the vehicle must be moved
Use the hazard lights instead of the parking brake for short stops
questions.e: Set the parking brake, shift to park, remove the key, and lock up.

questions.q: Which option correctly states a safe following distance in good conditions?
o: Half a car length
At least a 2-second gap
One car length at any speed
5 metres
questions.e: Keep at least a 2-second gap — more in poor weather — so you have time to react.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, in rain, snow, or fog you should increase your following distance to:
o: Exactly 2 seconds because lower speed provides enough stopping room
At least 3 to 4 seconds or more, depending on conditions
Exactly 5 seconds in every type of poor weather
One additional vehicle length regardless of speed
questions.e: Bad conditions need a larger gap — 3 to 4 seconds or more.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When must you turn your headlights on?
o: From sunset until sunrise, but not during poor daytime visibility
From one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise, and whenever visibility is poor
From one hour before sunset until one hour after sunrise in all conditions
Only when street lighting is not available
questions.e: Headlights are required during nighttime — one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise — and whenever conditions reduce visibility.

questions.q: Apply the Alberta rule to this situation. If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
o: Brake firmly and steer opposite the direction you want to travel
Ease off the accelerator and steer where you want the vehicle to go
Accelerate gently until the tires regain traction
Hold the steering wheel straight until the vehicle stops sliding
questions.e: Ease off the accelerator and steer where you want the front to go; avoid slamming the brakes.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, on a slippery or icy road, you should:
o: Use firm, repeated braking to test available traction
Slow down and increase your following distance
Maintain the posted speed but avoid lane changes
Follow the vehicle ahead more closely so you can copy its path
questions.e: Slow down and leave extra distance — stopping takes much longer on ice.

questions.q: Which description of hydroplaning is correct?
o: Your engine overheats
Tires ride up on water and lose grip
You brake too gently
You use high beams
questions.e: Hydroplaning is when tires lose contact by riding on a film of water; ease off the gas and don't brake hard.

questions.q: Which option correctly completes this safety rule? To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, you should:
o: Maintain speed so the tire tread clears water more quickly
Slow down and keep your tires properly inflated and in good condition
Brake lightly whenever you cross standing water
Steer toward the deepest tire tracks left by other vehicles
questions.e: Lower speed and good tires reduce hydroplaning risk.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, what should you check before changing lanes?
o: Mirrors only, provided they are adjusted correctly
Mirrors, signal, and a shoulder check of the blind spot
The lane ahead and the rear-view mirror only
The side mirror twice instead of performing a shoulder check
questions.e: Mirror, signal, then shoulder-check your blind spot before moving over.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, large trucks and buses have big blind spots. The safest approach is:
o: Remain beside the cab where the driver is most likely to notice you
Avoid lingering beside them; if you cannot see the driver's mirror, the driver may not see you
Pass on the right because the driver sits on the left
Follow closely so your headlights remain visible in the mirrors
questions.e: Stay out of the 'No-Zones'. If you can't see the driver in their mirror, they can't see you.

questions.q: Apply the Alberta rule to this situation. If you feel drowsy while driving, the safest thing is to:
o: Open a window and continue until the next scheduled stop
Pull over somewhere safe and rest
Drink caffeine and continue at a reduced speed
Change lanes frequently to stay mentally engaged
questions.e: Fatigue impairs driving — pull over and rest; music and air don't fix drowsiness.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes this rule? Using a hand-held cellphone while driving in Alberta is:
o: Permitted while fully stopped at a red traffic light
Illegal under distracted-driving law
Permitted for Class 5 drivers but not learners
Illegal only when the vehicle is travelling above 50 km/h
questions.e: Hand-held phone use is distracted driving — illegal, with a fine and demerit points.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When approaching a railway crossing with flashing red lights, you must:
o: Cross if the train is still more than one block away
Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed
Slow to 30 km/h and cross after checking both directions
Stop only when the crossing gate has lowered
questions.e: Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the way is clear — never try to beat a train.

questions.q: Before this action, which requirement applies? Before starting to drive, your first actions should be to:
o: Start moving, then adjust the mirrors once traffic is clear
Fasten your seatbelt and adjust your seat and mirrors
Check the dashboard after entering the roadway
Adjust only the rear-view mirror because side mirrors are checked while moving
questions.e: Buckle up and adjust your seat and mirrors before you move.

questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The safest way to handle a tailgater behind you is to:
o: Tap the brakes to show that the following distance is unsafe
Move over when safe and allow the vehicle to pass
Increase speed until a larger gap develops behind you
Maintain position and focus only on traffic ahead
questions.e: Let a tailgater pass when you safely can; don't brake-check or race.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When driving in fog, you should use:
o: High-beam headlights to illuminate farther ahead
Low-beam headlights to reduce reflected glare
Parking lights so other drivers can see your vehicle
Hazard lights together with high-beam headlights
questions.e: Low beams work better in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The recommended way to steer in normal driving is:
o: One hand near the 12 o’clock position
Both hands around 9 and 3, or another balanced low position
One hand low on the wheel while the other rests on the gear selector
Both hands close together at the top of the wheel
questions.e: Keep both hands on the wheel at balanced positions for control.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, 'Nighttime' in the Alberta Basic Licence Driver's Guide is defined as:
o: Sunset to sunrise
One hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
9 p.m. to 6 a.m.
When streetlights are on
questions.e: Officially, nighttime is one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise.

questions.q: While driving, you're being passed by another vehicle. You should:
o: Increase speed slightly so the passing vehicle spends less time beside you
Maintain a steady speed and allow the vehicle to complete the pass
Move toward the centre line to discourage an unsafe pass
Brake firmly as soon as the passing vehicle reaches your blind spot
questions.e: Hold your speed (or ease off slightly) so they can pass safely.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, cruise control is best avoided on:
o: Dry highways
Wet, icy, or slippery roads
Long straight roads
Flat ground
questions.e: Avoid cruise control on slippery roads where you may need full control.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When you plan to turn, you should signal:
o: Only after beginning to slow down
Well before the turn so other road users have time to react
Only when another vehicle is close enough to be affected
At the point where you begin turning the steering wheel
questions.e: Signal early, before slowing, to give others time to react.

questions.q: Apply the Alberta rule to this situation. If your brakes suddenly fail, one thing you can try is:
o: Switch off the ignition immediately while travelling at speed
Pump the brake pedal and downshift to help reduce speed
Apply the parking brake fully in one motion
Shift directly into park while steering to the shoulder
questions.e: Pump the pedal, shift to a lower gear, and use the parking brake gently; steer to a safe spot.

questions.q: While driving, your right wheels drift onto a soft shoulder. You should:
o: Steer sharply back onto the pavement before losing speed
Ease off the accelerator, slow down, and return gently to the road
Brake firmly while half of the vehicle remains on the pavement
Accelerate so the tires climb back over the pavement edge
questions.e: Don't jerk the wheel — slow down, then ease back onto the road smoothly.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When you approach a curve, you should:
o: Maintain speed until entering the curve, then brake as needed
Slow before the curve, then accelerate gently through it
Coast through the curve with the transmission in neutral
Move toward the centre line to reduce the sharpness of the curve
questions.e: Reduce speed before the curve, then power gently through for control.

questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The best defence against another driver's mistake is to:
o: Match the speed of surrounding traffic even when conditions are poor
Stay alert and maintain space around your vehicle
Follow closely enough to anticipate the other driver’s movement
Use the horn whenever another vehicle approaches your lane
questions.e: Defensive driving — space, attention, anticipating others — prevents most collisions.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, on a multi-lane road, slower traffic should generally keep:
o: Left
Right
Centre
Any lane
questions.e: Keep right except to pass; leave the left lane for passing.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When you're the first to arrive at a collision scene, you should:
o: Continue driving and report the location at the next safe stop
Stop if safe, call for help, and warn approaching traffic
Move injured people away from the vehicles before calling for help
Park in the travel lane so other drivers are forced to slow down
questions.e: Stop if safe, call 911, and warn traffic; don't move the injured unless there's danger.

questions.q: Which answer correctly gives the rule for many passengers may a Class 7 learner carry?
o: No passengers at all
Only family members
No more than the number of seatbelts
Up to 4 friends
questions.e: No more passengers than there are working seatbelts in the vehicle.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, who must wear a seatbelt in the vehicle?
o: Only the driver
Only front-seat riders
The driver and every passenger
Only passengers under 16
questions.e: The driver and all passengers must be properly buckled up.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, who is legally responsible for making sure passengers under 16 are buckled up?
o: The passenger once they can fasten the belt without help
The driver of the vehicle
The registered owner, even when someone else is driving
The child’s parent or guardian, even when absent
questions.e: The driver is responsible for ensuring passengers under 16 are properly secured.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, in Alberta, a child must ride rear-facing until at least:
o: 1 year of age, regardless of the seat limits
2 years of age or until reaching the seat manufacturer's rear-facing limit
18 kg (40 lb), regardless of age
6 years of age or until a booster seat fits
questions.e: Children ride rear-facing until at least age 2 or the seat's stated height/weight limit.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A forward-facing child car seat is required for children who are:
o: Under 6 years old, regardless of weight
Under 6 years old and 18 kg (40 lb) or less
Age 6 to 8 and shorter than 145 cm
Under 18 kg only when seated in the front passenger seat
questions.e: Children under 6 and under 18 kg (40 lb) must use a proper child car seat.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, booster seats in Alberta are:
o: Required until a child reaches 145 cm
Strongly recommended until the seatbelt fits properly, but not required by Alberta law
Required for every child between ages 6 and 12
Required only when the vehicle has lap-and-shoulder belts
questions.e: Booster seats aren't legally required in Alberta but are strongly recommended until the belt fits properly.
