questions.q: Which statement correctly completes this rule? The safest place for children under 13 to ride is:
o: The front passenger seat with the seat moved fully rearward
The back seat, using the restraint appropriate for the child
Either front or back when a booster seat is being used
The front seat whenever the passenger airbag can be disabled
questions.e: Children are safest in the back seat, especially with front airbags.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A seatbelt should be worn:
o: With the shoulder belt under the arm if it touches the neck
Across the chest and low across the hips
With the lap belt across the stomach and shoulder belt near the neck
Slightly loose so the body can move during a collision
questions.e: Wear the shoulder belt across the chest and the lap belt low and snug across the hips.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, outside a city, town or village, what is the default maximum speed on a primary highway unless a sign states otherwise?
o: 80 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
questions.e: Unless a sign sets a different limit, the default maximum on a primary highway outside an urban area is 100 km/h.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When backing a passenger vehicle to the left, where should the driver mainly look?
o: Over the left shoulder, with brief checks forward
Only in the left side mirror
Over the right shoulder for the entire manoeuvre
Only through the rear-view camera
questions.e: When backing left, look mainly over the left shoulder while making brief checks forward and around the vehicle.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A green right-turn arrow is displayed beside a red traffic light. What may a driver do?
o: Turn right in the arrow's direction when the way is safe
Go straight after slowing
Turn right only after the signal becomes fully green
Make either a right or left turn after stopping
questions.e: A green arrow permits movement in the arrow's direction even when another signal is red, but the driver must still proceed safely and yield where required.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A fully licensed Alberta driver normally receives a licence suspension after accumulating how many demerit points?
questions.e: A fully licensed driver is normally suspended at 15 demerit points. GDL drivers have a lower threshold.

questions.q: After this event, which response is correct? After passing a large truck on a two-way highway, when should you return to your lane?
o: As soon as your rear bumper clears the truck
After leaving extra space so the truck is clearly visible behind you
When the truck driver flashes the headlights
As soon as you can no longer see the truck's front wheels
questions.e: Large vehicles need more stopping room. Leave extra space before moving back into the lane ahead of a truck.

questions.q: Before this action, which requirement applies? Before turning right at a red light where the turn is permitted, what must you do?
o: Slow and turn without stopping when no vehicle is visible
Stop fully, check that the turn is permitted, yield, and turn only when safe
Stop only when pedestrians are present
Wait for a green light in every case
questions.e: A right turn on red requires a complete stop first. The driver must check for a prohibition and yield to traffic and pedestrians before turning.

questions.q: Which answer correctly explains a single solid white line separating lanes generally tell drivers?
o: Traffic is moving in opposite directions
Lane changes across the line are not permitted
Passing must occur on the right
The lane is reserved only during rush hour
questions.e: A solid white line generally means drivers should not change lanes across it.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, in a vehicle equipped with ABS, what should you do during an emergency stop?
o: Pump the brake pedal rapidly
Press the brake firmly and keep steering toward a safe path
Apply the parking brake first
Release the brake whenever the pedal vibrates
questions.e: With ABS, apply firm continuous brake pressure and steer as needed. Pedal vibration is normal; do not pump the brakes.

questions.q: Which answer correctly explains it mean to over-drive your headlights at night?
o: Using high beams longer than permitted
Driving too fast to stop within the distance illuminated ahead
Using headlights during daylight
Following another vehicle with headlights on
questions.e: You are over-driving your headlights when your stopping distance is longer than the distance you can see.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When parallel parked, how close must the wheels nearest the curb generally be?
o: Within 20 cm
Within 30 cm
Within 50 cm
Within 1 metre
questions.e: When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the curb should be no more than 50 centimetres from it.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When stopped behind another vehicle in traffic, what space should you leave?
o: Enough to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead and move out without reversing
Exactly one metre in all conditions
No more than half a vehicle length
Enough to see only the rear licence plate
questions.e: Leave enough room to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead and to move around it without first reversing.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A slow-moving vehicle emblem is intended for vehicles that normally travel at less than:
o: 30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
60 km/h
questions.e: The slow-moving vehicle emblem identifies vehicles that normally travel at less than 40 km/h.

questions.q: Which option correctly states a weave zone on a freeway?
o: A section where entrance and exit traffic must cross paths over a short distance
A series of sharp curves requiring alternating steering
A lane reserved for emergency vehicles
A shoulder area used by disabled vehicles
questions.e: A weave zone occurs where vehicles entering and leaving the freeway must cross paths within a limited distance.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A registry road test may be refused when the test vehicle is:
o: A rental vehicle
More than five years old
Mechanically unsafe
Equipped with an automatic transmission
questions.e: The vehicle used for a road test must be safe and roadworthy. An examiner may refuse an unsafe vehicle.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, may a driver exceed the posted speed limit while passing another vehicle?
o: Yes, by up to 10 km/h
Yes, but only on a divided highway
No, the speed limit still applies
Only when the passing lane is short
questions.e: The posted speed limit remains the maximum legal speed while passing.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When must a posted construction-zone speed limit be obeyed?
o: Only while workers are visible
Only during daylight hours
Whenever the limit is posted and in effect
Only while a flag person is controlling traffic
questions.e: Drivers must obey the posted construction-zone speed limit whenever it is in effect, not only when workers are visible.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, in a vehicle without ABS, what is threshold braking?
o: Pumping the brake pedal as rapidly as possible
Applying firm pressure just short of locking the wheels
Using only the parking brake
Locking the wheels and holding them locked
questions.e: Threshold braking uses the greatest braking force possible without locking the wheels.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, which technique produces a smooth normal stop?
o: Increase brake pressure continuously until the vehicle stops
Brake firmly, ease pressure slightly near the end, then finish the stop
Shift to neutral before touching the brake
Pump the brake pedal throughout the stop
questions.e: For a smooth stop, apply the brakes, ease pressure slightly just before stopping, then finish the stop gently.

questions.q: Which option correctly states the purpose of a freeway deceleration lane?
o: To build speed before entering the freeway
To reduce speed after leaving the through lane
To provide a lane for passing slow traffic
To stop and wait for a gap in freeway traffic
questions.e: Move into the deceleration lane before slowing so through traffic can continue at freeway speed.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road, which lane should you normally enter?
o: The lane nearest the right curb
The lane nearest the left curb
Any lane that appears clear
The centre lane when one exists
questions.e: A left turn from a two-way road onto a one-way road should normally finish in the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When backing straight, where should the driver mainly look?
o: Over the right shoulder through the rear window, while checking around the vehicle
Only at the rear-view camera
Over the left shoulder at all times
Only in both side mirrors
questions.e: For straight backing, look mainly through the rear window over the right shoulder while continuing to check the vehicle's surroundings.

questions.q: Which option correctly states an acceleration lane designed for?
o: Stopping before entering a freeway
Building speed to match freeway traffic before merging
Passing vehicles already on the freeway
Reducing speed before an exit
questions.e: Use an acceleration lane to reach a speed close to freeway traffic before merging into a safe gap.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, unless signs state different times, when are Alberta school-zone limits generally in effect on school days?
o: 8:30 a.m. until one hour after sunset
From sunrise to sunset
Continuously from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
questions.e: Unless otherwise posted, the standard school-zone periods are 8:00–9:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m., and 3:00–4:30 p.m. on school days.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A vehicle is trying to merge from an acceleration lane on your right. What should you do when possible?
o: Speed up to prevent it entering ahead
Maintain exactly the same position regardless of traffic
Move left if safe or adjust speed to help create a gap
Stop in the through lane
questions.e: Although the merging driver must find a safe gap, through drivers can improve safety by moving left when safe or adjusting speed.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When parking uphill beside a curb, which way should the front wheels be turned?
o: Toward the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
Parallel to the curb
questions.e: Uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle would roll back against the curb if it moved.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, in normal urban driving, how far ahead should a driver generally scan?
o: About 3 to 5 seconds
About 6 to 8 seconds
About 12 to 15 seconds
At least 30 seconds
questions.e: Looking about 12 to 15 seconds ahead helps a driver identify hazards early and plan smoothly.

questions.q: Under Alberta rules, as you approach the crest of a hill on a two-lane highway, where should you position your vehicle?
o: Close to the centre line
Toward the right side of your lane
Partly on the shoulder
In the oncoming lane if it appears clear
questions.e: Stay well to the right near a hill crest because an oncoming hazard may be hidden from view.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, what causes most vehicle skids?
o: Mechanical brake failure
Poor road design
Driver actions that exceed available traction
Snowfall by itself
questions.e: Most skids result from driver error, such as braking, steering, or accelerating too aggressively for available traction.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When may a vehicle legally occupy a designated disability parking space?
o: Whenever the driver remains inside
When nearby spaces are full
When it displays the proper disability placard or licence plate
For any stop shorter than five minutes
questions.e: A designated disability space may be used only by a vehicle displaying the required valid placard or plate.

questions.q: Apply the correct Alberta rule. At night, when following another vehicle, high beams should be dimmed when you are within approximately:
o: 60 metres
100 metres
150 metres
300 metres
questions.e: Dim high beams when following another vehicle within 150 metres so glare does not interfere with the other driver.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When are dual turns from more than one lane permitted?
o: Whenever both roads have multiple lanes
Only when signs or pavement markings indicate them
Whenever traffic is light
Only when directed by another driver
questions.e: Dual turns are permitted only where signs or pavement markings specifically authorize them.

questions.q: Which answer correctly explains a posted speed limit represent?
o: The speed every vehicle must maintain
The maximum speed under favourable road and weather conditions
A minimum speed for the lane
A limit that may be exceeded while passing
questions.e: A posted limit is the maximum under favourable conditions. Drivers must slow further when conditions make that speed unsafe.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, what makes an intersection uncontrolled?
o: It has traffic lights but no signs
It has stop signs on only one road
It has no traffic signs or traffic signals controlling right-of-way
It is controlled only during rush hour
questions.e: An uncontrolled intersection has no signs or signals assigning right-of-way. Drivers must apply the uncontrolled-intersection rules.

questions.q: Apply the correct Alberta rule. At night, high beams must be dimmed for an approaching vehicle when it is within approximately:
o: 60 metres
150 metres
300 metres
500 metres
questions.e: Dim high beams when an approaching vehicle is within 300 metres to avoid blinding the other driver.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, where should the centre of an adjustable head restraint be positioned?
o: At shoulder height
Near the top of the ears
At the base of the neck
Above the top of the head
questions.e: Position the centre of the head restraint near the top of the ears to reduce neck injury in a collision.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A slower vehicle reaches a passing-lane section. What should its driver do?
o: Stay in the left lane to prevent unsafe passing
Move to the right lane when safe and allow faster traffic to pass
Increase speed above the limit
Stop on the shoulder until all traffic passes
questions.e: Slower traffic should use the right lane in a passing-lane section and allow faster vehicles to pass safely.

questions.q: Before this action, which requirement applies? Before driving from a parking lot or driveway across a sidewalk and onto a roadway, a driver must:
o: Stop only if a sign is posted
Come to a complete stop and yield before entering
Continue slowly because roadway traffic must yield
Stop only when a pedestrian is visible
questions.e: A driver emerging from a parking lot, alley, or driveway must stop before crossing the sidewalk or entering the roadway and yield as required.

questions.q: Apply the correct Alberta rule. At a railway crossing with flashing red lights, how far from the nearest rail should you stop?
o: At least 2 metres
At least 3 metres
At least 5 metres
At least 15 metres
questions.e: Stop at least 5 metres from the nearest rail and wait until the warning stops and the crossing is safe.

questions.q: What makes it especially dangerous to pass a loaded log truck while it is turning?
o: The truck is not required to signal
The rear of the load can sweep across adjoining lanes
The truck must stop halfway through every turn
The driver cannot see vehicles in front
questions.e: The rear of a long load can swing or sweep across nearby lanes during a turn. Stay back and never try to squeeze past.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When angle parked, how close should the front wheel be to the curb?
o: Within 25 cm
Within 50 cm
Within 75 cm
Within 1 metre
questions.e: When angle parked, the front wheel should be no more than 50 centimetres from the curb.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A pedestrian at a crosswalk points an arm across the roadway. What should a driver understand?
o: The pedestrian is directing vehicles to continue
The pedestrian is indicating an intention to cross, so the driver must stop and yield
The pedestrian wants traffic to slow but not stop
The signal applies only to cyclists
questions.e: A pedestrian may signal an intention to cross by pointing an arm across the road. Drivers must stop and yield.

questions.q: Choose the correct response to this situation. A broken yellow centre line is beside a solid yellow line. When may you pass?
o: Only when the broken line is on your side and the pass is otherwise safe
Only when the solid line is on your side
From either direction whenever no vehicle is visible
Never from either direction
questions.e: Passing may be permitted for traffic beside the broken line, provided the manoeuvre is legal and safe. Traffic beside the solid line must not pass.

questions.q: Under Alberta driving rules, on a two-lane highway, which side should normally be used to pass a vehicle travelling in the same direction?
o: The right side
The left side when the pass is legal and safe
Either shoulder
Whichever side has more space
questions.e: Normally pass on the left when markings, sight distance, and traffic conditions allow it safely.

questions.q: A driver encounters this situation. When parking uphill on a road without a curb, which way should the front wheels be turned?
o: Toward the right edge of the roadway
Toward the centre of the roadway
Straight ahead
Either direction if the parking brake is set
questions.e: Uphill without a curb, turn the wheels toward the right edge so the vehicle would roll away from traffic if it moved.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? What is the minimum score needed to pass the Alberta Class 7 knowledge test?
o: 20 out of 30
23 out of 30
25 out of 30
28 out of 30
questions.e: You need 25 out of 30 (83%) correct.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? As a Class 7 learner, what blood alcohol level are you allowed while driving?
o: Under 0.05
Under 0.08
0.00 — zero
One drink is fine
questions.e: Class 7 learners must be at zero (0.00). The same zero rule covers cannabis and other drugs.

questions.q: Choose the correct completion under Alberta rules. A Class 7 learner must be accompanied by a supervising driver who is:
o: Any licensed driver
Fully licensed, 18 or older, in the front passenger seat
A GDL driver in the back seat
At least 16 years old
questions.e: Your supervisor must be a fully licensed (non-GDL) driver, 18+, seated beside you in front.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? At how many demerit points is a Class 7 learner's licence suspended?
o: 6 points
8 points
12 points
15 points
questions.e: GDL drivers are suspended at 8 demerit points — lower than the 15 for fully licensed drivers.

questions.q: Choose the correct completion under Alberta rules. A Class 7 learner is NOT permitted to drive between:
o: 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
Midnight and 5 a.m.
11 p.m. and 4 a.m.
Sunset and sunrise
questions.e: Learners may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? How often may you attempt the Alberta driver knowledge test?
o: Twice in a 24-hour period
Once per day
Once every 7 days
Three times per calendar month
questions.e: The knowledge test may be taken once per day, and the fee must be paid for each attempt.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? Can a Class 7 learner upgrade to a commercial licence (Class 1, 2, 3 or 4)?
o: Yes, anytime
No — not while in GDL
Yes, after passing a test
Only Class 4
questions.e: GDL drivers cannot hold or upgrade to a commercial licence.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? When can a Class 7 learner drive alone?
o: After holding the licence for 6 months
Never — a qualified supervising driver is required
After turning 16, but only during daylight hours
After completing an approved driver-training course
questions.e: A Class 7 learner can never drive alone; a qualified supervisor must always be beside you.

questions.q: Choose the correct completion under Alberta rules. To exit the GDL program and get a full Class 5 licence, you must first:
o: Be at least 18, complete the required probationary period, and be suspension- and demerit-free for the last 12 months
Pass an advanced road test after holding a Class 5-GDL licence for one year
Hold a Class 7 licence for 24 months without taking a Class 5 road test
Complete a commercial driver-training course and turn 18
questions.e: To exit GDL, you must be at least 18, complete the required probationary period, and be suspension- and demerit-free for the last 12 months. An advanced road test is no longer required.

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? What is the minimum age to get a Class 7 learner's licence in Alberta?
questions.e: You can get a Class 7 licence at 14 (with parent/guardian consent if under 18).

questions.q: Which answer is correct under Alberta driving rules? If you are under 18, what else do you need to apply for a Class 7 licence?
o: A job
Parent or guardian consent
A vehicle of your own
Two references
questions.e: Applicants under 18 need written parental or guardian consent.
